rationale: DART `cast_pattern` — the `X as T` form INSIDE A PATTERN (Dart 3 pattern grammar), which the completeness census carried as an uncovered construct type. Probed against the pinned grammar (`be07cf7`): `cast_pattern -> variable_pattern, as, type_identifier`, so the CAST TYPE is a `type_identifier` whose parent is `cast_pattern`; it occurs in a `switch_statement_case` and in an `if_case_clause` (`if (x case ...)`), and the fixture carries both positions. What this lane publishes, pinned here from a measured run: the pattern BINDING is a `uses` row binding-spelled `<callable>\u0000<binding>` at 0.9 with `isLocalRead` + `localBinding` (DARTGAP1: a pattern binding behaves as a parameter does, published as a use with no symbol behind it) and the CAST TYPE is a `references{isTypeMention,typePosition:cast_pattern}` row at 0.95, published only when the name binds to a type THE RUN CAN SEE — which is why the fixture declares `Payload` itself (casting to `num`/`String` in a fixture that does not declare dart:core would publish nothing, and a fixture cannot tell an absent emission from a GATED one). A cast pattern is NOT a declaration: no symbol, no contains, and the member read on the bound variable (`first.size`) stays `uses{isMemberRead}` with `receiverCause:receiverTypeUnknown` because a pattern binding is not typed by this analyzer.
